featured_reviews.name: deepak rajgar
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Best Pure Veg Spot in Neelkanth Business Park!

Lark is my go-to spot whenever I’m at Neelkanth Business Park. It’s a perfect mix of great taste, hygiene, and a professional yet cozy vibe.

Here’s why it’s a must-visit:

Signature Dishes: You have to try the Pineapple Shira—it’s sweet, rich, and has real fruit bits. For snacks, the Lark Special Idli (loaded with dry fruits) and Idli Chilly Fry are absolutely delicious and perfectly spiced.

Multi-Cuisine Variety: Their menu is huge! From authentic South Indian breakfast to spicy Chinese and North Indian Sizzlers, everything is fresh and flavorful. The Kerala Appam with Stew is another hidden gem here.

Cleanliness & Ambience: The restaurant is very well-maintained. The washrooms are clean, and the seating is comfortable enough for a quick lunch or a long team dinner.

Budget-Friendly: Despite being in a premium business park, the prices are very reasonable for the quality and quantity they serve.

Convenience: Located on the ground floor, it’s super accessible for everyone working in the park or coming from Vidya Vihar station.

Verdict: 5/5 for service, taste, and cleanliness. Definitely the best pure veg option in the area!

featured_reviews.name: Rajkumar Sahu
featured_reviews.review_text:
I stayed at Bougan Villa for 1 day, and overall it was a really pleasant and comfortable experience. From the moment I arrived, the staff was polite, welcoming, and helpful. The check-in process was smooth, and they guided me properly with all the basic information about the property.
The room was clean, well-maintained, and spacious, with a peaceful atmosphere that made the stay relaxing. The bedding was comfortable, and the room had all the necessary amenities required for a short stay. The washroom was also hygienic and neatly arranged, which is something I always appreciate while traveling.
One of the best things about Bougan Villa is the calm and quiet environment. It feels like a perfect place to unwind, especially if you want to stay away from noise and enjoy a peaceful time. The property is well managed, and everything felt organized.
The location is also good, and it was convenient for me to reach nearby places easily. I also liked the overall vibe of the hotel — it feels warm and homely rather than just a typical stay.
I would definitely recommend Bougan Villa to anyone looking for a clean, comfortable, and peaceful stay. I would love to visit again in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️
Good food, but the value for money really hurts – Bhagat Tarachand, Ghatkopar East

As a food blogger who eats out across Mumbai, I finally stopped by Bhagat Tarachand, Ghatkopar East after hearing so much about their consistent North Indian and Sindhi-style food. The taste did live up to the reputation – but the pricing and portion size left me honestly disappointed, hence this 3-star review.

Ambience & First Impressions

The outlet has a clean, family-restaurant vibe – bright lighting, compact seating and a steady flow of diners through the evening. It’s clearly a popular pure veg restaurant in Ghatkopar East for families and big groups, and service is quick and efficient even during peak hours.

You get that old-school Bhagat Tarachand feel – steel plates, homely gravies and attentive servers – but with the pricing and polish of a modern air-conditioned dine-in.

Food: Tasty, Comforting, Old-School Flavours

No complaints on the flavour front. The sabzis, phulkas and accompaniments all tasted homely and well-balanced. The greens we ordered (a saag / leafy veggie preparation with potatoes) was delicious – properly spiced, loaded with fresh methi/palak, and cooked in that classic, slightly rustic BT style.

Overall, this is the kind of food that pairs beautifully with hot phulkas, chaas and a relaxed family dinner. If you’re searching for North Indian veg food in Ghatkopar East, Bhagat Tarachand still knows how to deliver on taste.

The Big Let-down: ₹450 for a Limited Veg Thali

Where the experience really dipped for me was the pricing of the veg thali.
•	₹450 for a veg thali (limited, no refills)
•	Quantity felt modest – especially the sabzis and dal portions
•	For this price point, you naturally expect either generous servings or at least unlimited refills on core items (dal, sabzi, phulka/rice)

Unfortunately, this was a strictly limited thali, and the amount of food on the plate simply didn’t feel justified for ₹450 – especially when you compare it with other popular thali restaurants in Ghatkopar and across Mumbai that offer similar or better portions, often with refills, at a lower or comparable price.

As a diner, you walk out feeling that the value-for-money equation is off, even though your taste buds are happy.

Service

Service was polite and fairly quick – staff is used to handling heavy crowds and multiple thali orders at once. Water, accompaniments and roti service were prompt, and the servers are courteous and attentive without hovering.

No complaints on that front – the issue here is purely the pricing vs quantity, not the people or their hospitality.

Verdict: Worth It for Taste Once in a While, Not for Regular Visits

To sum it up:

Pros
•	Flavourful, satisfying vegetarian food
•	Classic Bhagat Tarachand style gravies and greens
•	Clean, family-friendly ambience in Ghatkopar East
•	Quick and polite service

Cons
•	₹450 for a limited veg thali feels exorbitant
•	Portion size does not justify the price
•	Overall experience feels expensive for what’s on the plate

If you’re a Bhagat Tarachand loyalist, you’ll enjoy the familiar taste and may not mind paying a premium once in a while. But as a value-conscious food lover exploring restaurants in Ghatkopar, I’d say come here knowing that you’re paying more for the brand and nostalgia than for sheer quantity.

Overall rating: 3/5 – tasty food, but the high price for a limited thali stops this from being a place I’d frequent regularly.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I rarely write reviews, but our experience at Bhagat Tarachand (Ghatkopar) was deeply disappointing and upsetting — especially because I visited with my mother, expecting a pleasant meal. From the moment we entered, we were made to sit right next to the washroom, despite other tables being available. Even more frustrating, people who arrived after us not only received the exact same order before us, but the attentiveness and service they received was noticeably different. The raita we were served was too tangy, so we politely requested a little sugar. It took the waiter 10 minutes just to bring that — something that should have taken seconds. Asking for extra rotis was another struggle. The staff showed visible reluctance and even attitude when we requested them, and again, they were brought very late. Throughout the meal, we felt neglected — as if our presence was an inconvenience and we weren’t paying customers. Every item we ordered was delayed or treated dismissively. The service we received made us feel like we were eating there for free. What made it worse was the clear difference in how we were treated compared to others. As both of us were wearing abaya's , it was hard to ignore the stark contrast in behavior and courtesy extended to us versus other diners. The sense of bias in the service was not just disappointing — it was hurtful. Restaurants should treat every customer with basic respect, regardless of appearance or attire. Sadly, that standard was not met here.

I hope the management takes this feedback seriously. No one should be made to feel unwelcome at a place meant for hospitality.

featured_reviews.name: Manoj Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Udupi 2 Mumbai in Vidyavihar (East), near the railway station on R.C. Marg, is a stellar pure-vegetarian destination offering authentic South Indian, North Indian, and Indo-Chinese cuisine. Known for its generous portions, hygienic environment, and flavorful dishes like Paneer Makhmali and Veg Club Sizzler, it is a perfect spot for families and students alike.
Located in Sai Vihar Co-op Housing Society, this restaurant is a hidden gem for those seeking delicious, budget-friendly, and quick service. The menu shines with classic Udupi staples, including perfectly crispy dosas, fluffy idlis, and robust sambar that tastes just like the traditional flavors of South India. The ambiance is modern yet comfortable, making it a great spot for a casual lunch or family dinner.
A standout experience highlighted in recent vlogs is the unique, fiery Veg Club Sizzler, which comes highly recommended. Another favorite is the Paneer Makhmali, which is consistently praised for being "soft as butter," making it a must-try for vegetarian lovers. Their menu is extensive, catering to various tastes with options that ensure everyone in a group finds something they enjoy.
The staff is generally attentive and the service prompt, making it convenient for, commuters and local residents near Vidyavihar Station. It provides excellent value for money with high-quality, fresh food. Whether you are looking for a quick, authentic breakfast of idli-vada or a hearty, diverse, multi-cuisine dinner, Udupi 2 Mumbai delivers a reliable and enjoyable dining experience. It is a fantastic, reliable vegetarian eatery in the heart of the eastern suburbs.

I am writing to bring to your notice an issue I faced during my visit to Guru Kripa Hotel, Ghatkopar (East), on Sunday 28/12/2025

I had ordered Rava Sada Dosa, but the dosa served to me was cold and did not contain the usual ingredients such as mirchi, coconut, or kaju pieces. Only coriander leaves were added as garnishing. It was essentially a plain dough dosa, which is not the standard preparation expected. Although the food quality was not satisfactory, I still consumed it to avoid wasting food.

When I humbly raised this concern at the counter, instead of addressing the food quality issue, the person at the counter instructed the service boy to switch off the AC, implying that keeping the AC off would keep the food hot. This response felt inappropriate and showed a lack of concern for improving food quality. It also appeared unfair to other customers, as comfort was compromised instead of service being improved.

I also noticed that despite it being a Sunday (usually a busy day), there were hardly 10 customers present, which made me wonder if service issues could be a reason.

I am not writing this complaint with any ill intention. My humble request is that proper supervision be maintained, food quality be checked before serving, and customer concerns be handled respectfully. Such improvements will help maintain the reputation of your restaurant.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Studying engineering opens you up to several career options. However, one you may not have considered is opening up an engineer-themed bagel food truck in Mumbai. Not to worry though - B.E. Bytes (Hingwala Ln, Saibaba Nagar, Pant Nagar, Ghatkopar East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400077) has you covered to show you exactly what a successful venture looks like! A delicious food truck on the side of Ghatkopar's iconic road, this place served one of the best bagels I have ever had!
Since I wanted to sample several dishes from the nearby Khau Galli, I ordered a half-size Italian Bagel so that I didn't fill up early on. Picture this bagel as a well-designed circuit board, with each vegetable strategically placed like components on a motherboard.
The pizza sauce, akin to a carefully calculated algorithm, added a burst of tangy brilliance that harmonised with the intricate network of flavors. With the creaminess of the in-house cheese sauce mixed in with the exotic vegetables, each bite of this bagel was engineered to perfection, proving that even in the culinary world, precision and creativity can coexist like a seamlessly integrated system.
B.E. Bytes at Hingwala Lane is not just a food truck; it's an engineering marvel in the culinary landscape of Mumbai. So, whether you're exploring career options or simply seeking a delectable experience, B.E. Bytes IS the perfect pitstop for a taste of innovation in the vegetarian (and Jain) foodie haven of Mumbai. Highly recommended!

To hear more about this review, follow us @eatinontario on Instagram, TikTok, & Facebook. ✨🤩🙏

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

What makes it even better is that the entire restaurant is fully air-conditioned, making dining here a pleasant experience even on hot days. The place is clean, well-maintained, and comfortable for families as well as groups of friends.

The service is quick, polite, and efficient — exactly what you’d expect from a traditional Udipi restaurant.

If you’re looking for genuine South Indian food in Matunga that combines great taste, comfort, and a welcoming vibe, this is definitely one of the best spots to visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: vru
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Udupi Shri Krishna Restaurant, which is conveniently located just a 1-minute walk from Matunga East Railway Station—making it extremely easy to reach without any hassle.

I learned that the restaurant was inaugurated by Sane Guruji, which adds a nice historical and cultural touch to the place.

When we arrived, we had to wait in the coupon queue, but it was quite smooth. Within about 10 minutes, our name was called. Considering it was a Saturday, the waiting time was very reasonable. I’ve heard that sometimes the wait can go up to 45 minutes to an hour, but we were lucky.

The staff at the counter was very polite and attentive. One thing that stood out was how they reminded everyone to wash their hands before eating—such a small yet thoughtful and caring gesture.

The food is served on a banana leaf, which adds a traditional and authentic feel. The entire meal felt fresh, simple, and very much like home-cooked food.

The thali included:

2 sabjis
1 koshimbir (cucumber salad)
Roti and puri
Curd
Pickle
Buttermilk
Nimbu rasam and regular rasam
Rice with ghee
One sweet (options like rasgulla, halwa, shrikhand, or gulab jamun)

Curd and sweets are limited, while the rest is unlimited.

The taste was excellent—especially the curd and nimbu rasam, which were absolutely delicious. The rasgulla we had was fresh, mildly sweet, and exceeded expectations.

The management and service were top-notch. The staff ensured that hot food was served in every round, which made the experience even better. Overall, it truly felt like having a comforting meal at home.

The full thali costs ₹300, and the mini thali is ₹200, which is quite reasonable for the quality and quantity offered.

My only suggestion would be to introduce a premium thali option at a slightly higher price, including a few more South Indian dishes for those who want to explore more variety.

Overall, a wonderful experience—highly recommended to everyone! 👍

featured_reviews.name: DV
featured_reviews.review_text: This is an iconic eatery that is as old as 84 years. It's is a true treasure for Mumbaikars who like South Indian vegetarian food. It serves a full unlimited meal from the south Indian cuisines with Tamil dishes being prominently cooked and served. It's traditionally served on a banana leaf making it visually appealing. The Thali as it is known has Rasam, Sambar, Dal, Rice with option of ghee atop, Poori, Chapati, 2 dry cooked vegetables and 2 gravy based vegetables. There is curd and flavoured (ginger/coriander) butter milk. There is a choice of dessert; my favourite is the Moong Dal payasam. At a modest 300/- bucks it's absolutely value for money. It's a living testament of cultural bonding between the South Indian community and the local Maharashtrians as well as Gujratis. The fact that it was inaugurated by Sane Guruji makes it even richer in identity.

We visited during the Christmas season, so we got to try some festive specials. Mom enjoyed a non-alcoholic sangria, while I had a strawberry soda. We also loved the strawberry kale salad, which was too yummy!!

For starters, we had in a variety of dishes, including Korean paneer, Korean potatoes, crispy corn, dimsums, lime mushroom and much more. For mains we had a pasta that was made with coconut milk. (Unfortunately there are no aesthetic pictures cause we ate all the food as soon as it reached the table)

We had a basque cheesecake and a skillet cookie with vanilla soft serve for dessert. It was too yummy. Only complaint is that we were too full to try more desserts.

Before leaving, we spotted a tempting spread of cookies and pastries in the cafe section downstairs. We packed a few to enjoy the next day.

Overall, Bom Dia offers a beautiful combination of great food, anmazig offerings, and a warm, inviting ambiance.

Whether you’re dining in, celebrating something special, or picking up treats to go, it’s definitely a place I’d highly recommend and happily return to!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Madras is one of the most iconic South Indian restaurants in Mumbai and truly lives up to its reputation. Located in the heart of Matunga, this place is famous for serving authentic and delicious South Indian food with consistent quality for decades. The moment you enter, the aroma of fresh filter coffee, ghee, and spices creates a warm and nostalgic feeling.
I tried their famous dosa and idli, and both were excellent. The dosa was perfectly crispy with a flavorful potato filling, while the idli was soft, fresh, and served with tasty chutneys and sambhar. Their filter coffee was another highlight — strong, aromatic, and refreshing. Despite being crowded most of the time, the service is quick and efficient, which is impressive.
The restaurant maintains cleanliness and has a simple yet traditional atmosphere that adds to the experience. Prices are also reasonable considering the quality and popularity of the food. Overall, Cafe Madras is a must-visit place for anyone who loves authentic South Indian cuisine. It perfectly combines taste, tradition, and quality, making every visit memorable.

featured_reviews.review_text:
An iconic South Indian cuisine restaurant in the iconic Matunga east neighbourhood of Mumbai. Everything, I repeat, every damn food item here is par excellence.

Things eaten: Paniyaram, Rassam, Medu Vada, Kanchipuram idli, appam with coconut stew, mysore onion dosa, cheese pav bhaji, pineapple sheera AND filter coffee.

Verdict: The Medu vada is truly one of the best I have ever had. It is so soft yet crispy at the same time. The coconut chutney and Tamilian sambar is unparalleled. Appam with coconut stew is amazing as well. Especially the stew was so delicious. Mysore onion dosa feels rich in flavour and is prepared in pure ghee. Kanchipuram idli was a decent one and a bit sour. Paniyaram was a one-of-a-kind and is a must try. Cheese pav bhaji was not bad but failed to meet the bar raised by other food items. For desserts, you have to have the pineapple sheera and you can thank me later. A south indian cuisines is incomplete with the iconic filter coffee and the coffee here will not disappoint you. The service is super quick and they serve you unlimited Sambar and Chutney

This restaurant was hitting home-runs after home-runs and I was about to give this place the coveted 5-star rating when they committed a hygienic blunder. I found a small hair in their Pav. Hygiene is as important as the taste and had they not compromised on the hygiene, my search for the 5-starred restaurant would have ended today. But alas the search continues!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Cafe Mysore, Matunga with high expectations as it’s one of the well-known South Indian spots in Mumbai. Unfortunately, the experience didn’t quite live up to the hype.
We tried the Gadbad Idli, which sounded interesting on the menu, but taste-wise it was quite average and not up to the mark. The flavors felt unbalanced and it lacked the authentic punch you expect from a classic Matunga eatery.
We also ordered the Dilkhush Dosa (stuffed). The presentation was decent, but again, the taste didn’t justify the reputation or the pricing. It felt heavy and not particularly flavorful.
What disappointed us more was the customer service. The staff seemed disinterested and inattentive, which affected the overall dining experience. When a place carries such a strong reputation, basic hospitality should match the food quality.
Overall, in my opinion, it feels a bit overhyped. There are other South Indian restaurants in Matunga that offer better taste and service at similar or better prices.
Would consider revisiting only if there’s noticeable improvement.

featured_reviews.name: DNB Travel & Food Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
Classic South Indian Favourite with Great Food but Limited Parking

Review:
Cafe Mysore is one of Matunga’s iconic South Indian eateries — an institution famed for its authentic idlis, dosas, rasam vada, and filter coffee that have been delighting locals and food lovers for generations. The food is fresh, hearty, and very reasonably priced, making it a go-to breakfast or lunch spot for both regulars and first-timers. The dosa varieties (especially Dilkhush, Mysore masala) and pineapple sheera are often recommended by customers.

The ambience is casual and simple — not fancy, but clean and welcoming. It’s often busy during peak times (especially weekends and mornings), so be prepared for a bit of a crowd and sharing tables, which contributes to its classic local charm.

What We Loved 👍
Authentic South Indian flavours with generous portions.

Quick service most of the time for breakfast and tiffin items.

Pocket-friendly pricing.

Good for family breakfasts and casual meets.

Seating and comfort are basic; the place fills up quickly during rush hours.

Parking & Access 🚗
There is no dedicated parking lot or valet service at the cafe itself.

Being right on Matunga’s King’s Circle area, finding street parking can be challenging, especially during peak morning and evening hours. You may need to park in nearby public parking areas or use paid parking zones near the circle and walk a short distance.

If driving isn’t convenient, the cafe is very well connected by local transport, with King’s Circle railway station just a short walk away.

Best For: Authentic South Indian breakfast/lunch, quick meals, family outings, casual meet-ups.
